record.context_brief: MDM uniqueness under induced target set
record.original_question: Fix r > 0. A maximal distance minimizer (also called an r-minimizer) for a compact set M \subset \mathbb{R}^d is a connected compact set \Sigma of minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H^1(\Sigma)) among connected compact sets satisfying M \subset B_r(\Sigma), where B_r(\Sigma) is the closed r-neighborhood of \Sigma. Suppose \Sigma is an r-minimizer for some compact set M. Consider the maximal distance minimization problem with target set taken to be B_r(\Sigma). Is \Sigma the unique r-minimizer for B_r(\Sigma)?

evidence.quote:
For a given compact set M ⊂ Rd and a given positive number r > 0, consider the problem of finding a connected compact
set Σ of minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H1 ) such that

                                M ⊂ Br (Σ),

where Br (Σ) denotes the closed r-neighborhood of the set Σ. We refer to such a set Σ as a Maximal distance minimizer
(MDM or r-minimizer).

Question 1.5. Let Σ be an r-minimizer for some M . Is Σ the unique r-minimizer for Br (Σ)?
     Clearly that if Σ is an r-minimizer for some M , then it is a minimizer for Br (Σ), see [2]. A weaker form of this question
is if we replace r with some positive r0 < r in the hypothesis.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a real number $r>0$ and a dimension $d\geq 2$. For a nonempty compact set $M\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, define a maximal distance minimizer (or $r$-minimizer) for $M$ to be a connected compact set $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ that minimizes the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1(\Sigma)$ among all connected compact sets satisfying
$$M\subset B_r(\Sigma):=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:\operatorname{dist}(x,\Sigma)\leq r\}.$$
Suppose that $\Sigma$ is an $r$-minimizer for some compact set $M\subset\mathbb{R}^d$. Consider now the maximal distance minimization problem with target set $B_r(\Sigma)$ (i.e., minimize $\mathcal{H}^1(\Sigma')$ among connected compact sets $\Sigma'$ with $B_r(\Sigma)\subset B_r(\Sigma')$). Is $\Sigma$ necessarily the unique $r$-minimizer for $B_r(\Sigma)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recent compilation of open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers (2025). Surveys on the topic discuss uniqueness questions for $r$-minimizers but do not provide a resolution to this specific self-induced target uniqueness question.
